articles.title: Retrospectively Reverse-Engineering Apple's Neural Engine
articles.summary: The Apple Neural Engine (ANE) was a custom-designed neural processing unit (NPU) for Apple's iPhones and Macs, but its architecture was too opinionated to be used as a general-purpose accelerator platform. The ANE's compute core was designed for dense image-processing CNN workloads, but it also had a large parallel array of MAC units that could accelerate other types of workloads. The ANE's datapath, which includes dataflow surrounding the MACs, was optimized for transformers, a type of neural network that was popular in 2017. The M5 decision, which confirmed that the ANE's compute core remained useful for transformers, suggests that the ANE's architecture was designed to support a specific type of workload, and that it was not as versatile as it seemed.

articles.title: Pandas Should Go Extinct
articles.summary: Pandas' inefficiencies force users to adopt distributed querying systems before workloads justify the added complexity, leading to a well-marketed "silver bullet" that is just a marketing gimmick. The typical adoption pathway for Pandas shows a rough guide of when to consider adopting a given library based on data size, with Pandas serving users well into the 10s of GBs range before hitting memory issues and slow computation. A gap exists between the "Pandas cliff" and the scale where distributed systems are genuinely necessary, around the 100GB mark, which can be effectively filled by modern tools like Polars and DuckDB.
